correctness.rationale: The statement quantifies over all nonempty sets and arbitrary local normal filters, including infinite nonprincipal filters. In the pointwise direction, a mixed proper/improper pair is refuted by the empty valuation; for proper nonreflexive local neighborhoods, a rectangle U×V makes product necessity true while the opposite coordinate slice is empty and cannot be supported by a proper filter. The T/T and improper/improper implications are immediate from witness rectangles and empty members, respectively. Fixing one product point propagates the local dichotomy across every x and y. For finite X and Y, each filter is principal and has an arbitrary subset generator; the count is \(2^{n(n-1)+m(m-1)}+1\). The standalone checker examines every finite frame pair, valuation and product point for sizes 1x1, 1x2, 2x2, 2x3, with 4, 32, 256, 8192 pairs and 2, 5, 17, 257 valid respectively. No infinite result is inferred from these finite checks.

value.rationale: The 2026 source explicitly identifies sub as central to the difference between topological/T products and D products. The new theorem resolves the exact object-level boundary for every pair of arbitrary normal neighborhood factors, including infinite nonprincipal cases, rather than presenting another isolated non-T counterexample: D-factor validity is equivalent to factorwise T, with a unique nonserial/global degeneration. This complete classification also produces the exact natural labeled-frame census and density for all two positive carrier sizes; the +1 term is a meaningful semantic boundary caused by inconsistent local filters. The result is a structural iff, not an arbitrary parameter substitution or mere correct computation.
